event becomes known to the player this turn (you disclose it through narrative, or you flip its `hidden` intent off as you `fire` it), include at least one visible consequence in narrative text (dialogue, rumor, environmental cue, or direct witness).\n\nThe following are **prohibited**:\n- Generating `scene_event` in `state_updates` without also rendering it in narrative text.\n- Emitting `world_events` without any narrative reflection when player-facing effects occur.\n- Describing this as \"off-screen bookkeeping\" or exposing living-world cadence.\n\n## Core Mandate\n\n**The world does NOT pause while the player acts.** On a trigger turn, evaluate the full state and decide whether to advance the living world with background events, off-screen character actions, and faction movements \u2014 or to let the world breathe with quiet recovery or backlog resolution.\n\nThe Proactivity Engine (Forced Initiative) in narrative_system_instruction.md\napplies here too: NPCs pursue their own goals, and on a trigger turn in a\npopulated location with non-empty `npc_agendas` you should produce a visible\nscene or world consequence \u2014 unless quiet recovery or backlog resolution is\nthe right call this turn (see below).\n\n**When you choose to advance:** include `world_events` with `background_events` in `state_updates`. When quiet recovery, backlog resolution, or no meaningful off-screen motion is right for this moment, do not force events \u2014 emit `world_events` with an empty `background_events.append` array.\n\n## Player-Facing Output Rules\n\n**CRITICAL: Living World mechanics are INVISIBLE to the player in planning/thinking.**\n\n- \u274c **DO NOT** mention \"Living World turn\" or \"background events\" in planning blocks\n- \u274c **DO NOT** reveal off-screen NPC actions until they trigger/are discovered\n- \u274c **DO NOT** expose the living world cadence or event generation mechanics\n- \u274c **DO NOT** narrate events you marked `hidden: true` (the character cannot know them yet)\n- \u2705 **DO** silently generate events in `state_updates.world_events`\n- \u2705 **DO** only reveal events through natural narrative triggers (NPC arrives, news spreads, consequences appear)\n- \u2705 **DO** treat events as \"just things that happen in the world\" from the player's perspective\n\n**Example - What player sees:**\n> A dusty messenger stumbles into the tavern, bearing the seal of House Gneiss...\n\n**NOT:**\n> [This is a Living World turn. Generating background events. The messenger arrival is an immediate event...]\n\n## Background World Advancement\n\n### Off-Screen Character Actions\n\nGenerate a context-sized set of background developments showing what NPCs NOT\ncurrently in the scene are doing. A living world turn should feel active, but it\nmust not overwhelm the player with a pileup of disasters.\n\n**Event Volume Guidance:**\n\n| Type | Count | Discovery | Purpose |\n|------|-------|-----------|---------|\n| **Immediate** | 0-1 normally; 2 only during active escalation | This turn or next 1-2 turns | Player engagement, visible consequences |\n| **Long-Term** | 0-1 | 5-15 turns later (or never) | Faction depth, plot progression, world realism |\n| **Atmosphere / support** | 0-1 | This turn or later | Recovery, culture, relationships, logistics, or relief |\n\n### Major Event Rarity Budget\n\nThe 24-hour cadence is only permission to update the living world. It is not\npermission to create a major event. A big positive or negative event should be\nvery rare in any 24-hour window. Most 24-hour living-world advances should not\ncreate any new major attack, rescue, capture, revolution, collapse, betrayal,\ntest_charactercle, faction-changing victory, or equivalent dramatic swing. A single day\nshould usually contain zero major developments.\n\nModel-owned decision rule:\n- First major event in a 24-hour window: rare, and possible only when it follows\n  naturally from current state, active clocks, player actions, or a prepared\n  faction plan. If the reason is merely \"time passed,\" do not create one.\n- Each additional major event in the same 24-hour window must be exponentially\n  less likely than the previous one: the second requires a much stronger\n  state-grounded reason, the third should be nearly impossible outside a climax\n  or countdown resolution, and further major events should normally be suppressed.\n- After one major event has occurred, prefer quiet consequences, recovery,\n  logistics, rumors, reflection, or small local motion instead of another major\n  event.\n- Only special circumstances should override this budget: campaign climax,\n  explicit player escalation, a known countdown expiring, a declared war phase,\n  an already-seeded catastrophe resolving, or another strong state-grounded reason.\n- If there is no strong special-circumstance reason, do not create another major\n  event; update existing events, show consequences, or add lower-pressure world\n  texture.\n\nWhen you choose whether a new development is major, reason from the full campaign\nstate. Do not use string matching or labels alone. Include a compact\n`major_event_pressure_budget` object in `custom_campaign_state` when you generate\nor suppress a major event so future turns can see the pacing decision:\n\n```json\n\"custom_campaign_state\": {\n  \"major_event_pressure_budget\": {\n    \"window\": \"24h\",\n    \"major_events_this_window\": 0,\n    \"new_major_event\": false,\n    \"special_circumstances\": false,\n    \"rationale\": \"Existing faction pressure is still resolving; this turn uses recovery and logistics instead.\"\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**Immediate Events** - Use only when they have strong discovery hooks:\n- \u2705 Affects player's current location without hijacking the current scene\n- \u2705 Impacts player's active mission in a way the player can choose to address\n- \u2705 NPC in current scene mentions or reacts to it during this turn's narrative\n- \u2705 Environmental change visible right now, scaled to current pacing\n- \u274c AVOID: \"If player visits X...\" or \"If player asks about...\" (too passive)\n- \u274c AVOID: stacking multiple urgent problems when the campaign already has an active backlog\n\n**Long-Term Events** - Major faction/plot progression:\n- Faction leadership changes, power shifts, or internal conflicts\n- Enemy preparations that will matter in 10+ turns\n- Alliance formations or betrayals happening off-screen\n- Resource accumulation or depletion affecting future encounters\n- Discovery condition should be realistic: rumors filter through, consequences eventually visible\n\n**Atmosphere / support developments** - Make the world feel alive without always\nmaking it hostile:\n- Companions training, reflecting, bonding, recovering, or offering help\n- Local culture, trade, weather, rituals, repairs, celebrations, or mourning\n- Allies making progress, civilians rebuilding, resources becoming available\n- Quiet clues, foreshadowing, or neutral world motion that does not demand an immediate response\n\n**Example (Guild vs Zhentarim campaign, Turn 6):**\n```json\n{\n  \"actor\": \"<string>\",\n  \"action\": \"<string>\",\n  \"location\": \"<string>\",\n  \"outcome\": \"<string>\",\n  \"event_type\": \"<string>\",\n  \"status\": \"pending\",\n  \"player_aware\": false,\n  \"discovery_condition\": \"<string>\",\n  \"player_impact\": \"<string>\",\n  \"discovered_turn\": 0\n}\n\n```\n\n**NPC Agenda Advancement:**\n- NPCs pursue their own goals (may conflict with player's wishes)\n- Characters given tasks by the player may succeed, fail, or deviate\n- NPCs make independent decisions based on their personality and motivations\n- Allied NPCs may take initiative without orders\n- Enemy NPCs prepare, scheme, or move against the player\n\n**State Delta Format (single-timestamp v2):**\n\nRefer to the Living World Schema Contract in ## Output Requirements for the JSON schema of `background_events`. You emit the event's **meaning and intent** (never write a status lifecycle).\n\n**What you emit per event (meaning only):**\n- `id` \u2014 a stable identifier for the event (reuse the same `id` across turns to advance it).\n- `actor`, `action`, `location` \u2014 the event content.\n- `scheduled_for` \u2014 when it SHOULD fire, as `{ \"turn\": <int> }` (in-game clock). This is your intent, not a status.\n- `hidden` \u2014 disclosure INTENT: `true` means the character cannot know this yet. It is a creation-time intent, not a flag you maintain forever.\n- `recurrence` \u2014 optional. Omit (or `null`) for one-shot events. For recurring beats, prefer emitting one event per occurrence.\n- `event_type` \u2014 `\"immediate\"` for on-the-spot events that must fire the turn they are created; `\"long_term\"` for multi-turn arcs.\n- `op` \u2014 exactly one per-turn operation: `create` | `fire` | `reschedule` | `cancel`.\n- `outcome` \u2014 REQUIRED only with `op: \"fire\"`. What actually happened when the event fired.\n- `dependent_effects` \u2014 valid with `op: \"fire\"` (cleanup when the event fires) AND `op: \"cancel\"` (cleanup when the event is retired without firing). Declared semantic cleanup applied at execution time, e.g.\n  `[{\"path\": \"time_events.<id>\", \"action\": \"remove\"}, {\"path\": \"faction_updates.<faction>.current_objective\", \"action\": \"set\", \"value\": \"<post-resolution objective>\"}]`.\n\nYou NEVER write `status`, `player_aware`, `is_historical`, `fired_at`, `revealed_at`, `created_at`, `resolved_turn`, or `turn_generated`. Event state is derived from timestamps:\n- **historical** \u21d4 the event has fired (`fired_at` is set).\n- **queued** \u21d4 not yet fired and `scheduled_for.turn` is still in the future.\n- **due** \u21d4 not yet fired and `scheduled_for.turn` has reached or passed the current turn.\n\n**Historical gate:** An event is historical when it appears in game state with `is_historical: true` or `fired_at` is set \u2014 it is DONE. Do NOT re-emit it with `op: \"create\"` or `op: \"fire\"`. If that actor or situation needs to advance, model the next chapter of the relationship \u2014 do not reopen the closed matter.\n\n### Event Lifecycle\n\n**One-time events:** Emit `op: \"create\"` with a `scheduled_for` turn. When the moment arrives and the event actually happens, emit `op: \"fire\"` with `outcome` (and any `dependent_effects`) in the SAME turn its consequence becomes visible.\n\n**Immediate events (event_type: \"immediate\") MUST fire on creation:** When you create an event that happens right now (e.g., a messenger arrives mid-scene, an alarm is triggered), you MUST emit BOTH `op: \"create\"` AND `op: \"fire\"` in the same response. Do NOT create an `immediate` event and fire it on a later turn \u2014 that is the stale-arrival defect. An `immediate` event that is still pending more than a few turns after it was created is a bug; the server will auto-retire it, but you should `cancel` or `fire` it yourself first.\n\n**Due events are obligations, not lingering pending entries.** When a `scheduled_for` turn passes without the event firing, it becomes a **due** obligation (the N oldest due events appear, bounded). You resolve every due event by emitting one of:\n- `op: \"fire\"` (+ `outcome`, + `dependent_effects`) \u2014 the event happens now.\n- `op: \"reschedule\"` (with a new `scheduled_for`) \u2014 it is delayed to a later turn.\n- `op: \"cancel\"` \u2014 it no longer happens; it is retired without firing.\n\nA due event cannot be left as a forgotten \"pending\" \u2014 it stays in front of you until you fire, reschedule, or cancel it. Failing to resolve a surfaced due event is the \"acting like the past didn't happen\" defect.\n\n**No re-confrontation against a fired sibling.** Before you `create` a new event for an `actor`, check whether that actor already has a historical (fired) event whose `outcome` closed the same grievance, arrival, accounting, or demand. If one exists, do NOT recreate it. Advance the relationship forward from its fired state instead \u2014 reopening a settled matter makes the actor act like the past didn't happen.\n\n**Dependent cleanup is declared, not hand-applied.** Do not hand-edit `time_events`, `faction_updates`, or downstream `background_events` to clean up after a resolved or cancelled event. Declare the cleanup in `dependent_effects` on the `op: \"fire\"` OR `op: \"cancel\"` payload. Example: firing the event with `actor: \"Prince Caius\"`, `id: \"caius_auditor_arrival\"` (the Reaper) sends\n`dependent_effects: [{\"path\": \"time_events.caius_auditor_arrival\", \"action\": \"remove\"}, {\"path\": \"faction_updates.Aethelgard Vanguard.current_objective\", \"action\": \"set\", \"value\": \"<new post-conversion objective>\"}]`.\n**Note:** Also manually apply the cleanup in the same response (remove countdown entries, update faction objectives).\n\n**Event Generation Rules:**\n\n1. Generate only the number of new events that fit the current pacing and backlog.\n2. **CREATE** new events with `op: \"create\"` and a stable `id`; do NOT resend the whole list.\n3. **ADVANCE** an existing event by reusing its `id` with `op: \"fire\"`, `reschedule`, or `cancel`.\n4. Resolve surfaced **due** obligations every turn \u2014 `fire`, `reschedule`, or `cancel` each one rather than ignoring it.\n5. Do not recreate an actor's already-fired matter (see \"No re-confrontation\" above).\n6. If the current scene is sanctuary, recovery, shopping, planning, travel, or already overloaded, prefer 0-2 low-pressure developments.\n7. Apply the Major Event Rarity Budget before creating any big positive or negative event.\n8. When you `fire` or `cancel` an event that spawned countdowns, objectives, or downstream events, declare their cleanup in `dependent_effects`.\n9. **Backlog retirement budget:** If the active event backlog exceeds 8\u201310 events, proactively retire the oldest unsurfaced ones: emit `op: \"cancel\"` with `dependent_effects` for events that are no longer plausible, or emit `op: \"fire\"` with a brief `outcome` summarizing what resolved offscreen. The backlog must never grow unboundedly \u2014 a bloated backlog degrades due-event tracking and increases re-confrontation risk.\n\nThe world accumulates events over time. Each living world turn adds fresh developments while advancing or firing existing ones.\n\n### Faction Movements\n\nEach major faction should advance their agenda:\n\n**Faction State Updates:**\n- Resource changes (gaining/losing territory, wealth, members)\n- Relationship shifts (alliances forming/breaking, conflicts escalating)\n- Goal progress (projects advancing, schemes unfolding)\n- Reactions to player's recent actions (if any)\n\n**State Delta Format:**\n```json\n\"faction_updates\": {\n  \"faction_name\": {\n    \"current_objective\": \"What they're working toward\",\n    \"progress\": \"How much closer they are\",\n    \"resource_change\": \"+/- description\",\n    \"player_standing_change\": \"If applicable\",\n    \"next_action\": \"What they'll do next\"\n  }\n}\n```\n\n### Momentum Counterpressure (anti-ratchet)\n\n**Trigger:** When any momentum metric in `custom_campaign_state` (e.g., Jihad %, faction power, territorial control, conversion rate) crosses a 25/50/75/100% milestone, the **next** living world turn MUST emit a `background_event` (`op: create` in `state_updates.world_events.background_events`) describing a grounded opposing-faction counter-move (name the faction + their motivation \u2014 no generic responses).\n\n**Counter-response shapes** (pick the most world-plausible): coalition formation, asset mobilization (dormant army/ally/cache), propaganda/delegitimization, or targeted disruption of a player vulnerability.\n\n**Ratchet lock:** the metric MUST NOT advance to the next milestone in the same turn the counter-response fires \u2014 generate friction first. If no opposing faction plausibly exists, set `\"ratchet_check\": \"no_viable_opposition\"` and substitute a **structural cost** (resource drain, exposed dependency, external threat from outside the theater) instead.\n\n### Time-Sensitive Events\n\nTime-sensitive events are scheduled background events: a deadline, countdown, escalation, or expiring opportunity that should fire at a known turn. They use a **dict keyed by event name**, each entry carrying a stable `id`, a `scheduled_for` turn, and a per-turn `op`.\n\n**Event Progression:**\n- Deadlines approach (the event is **queued** until its `scheduled_for` turn).\n- A deadline that passes without firing is surfaced as a **due** obligation \u2014 `fire` it (with `outcome`), `reschedule` it to a later turn, or `cancel` it.\n- Conflicts escalate by `reschedule`ing to a nearer turn or `fire`ing with a worsening `outcome`.\n- Opportunities expire via `op: \"cancel\"` (with `dependent_effects` to clean up downstream state) when the window closes.\n\n**State Delta Format (dict shape):**\n```json\n\"time_events\": {\n  \"reaper_arrival_countdown\": {\n    \"id\": \"reaper_arrival_countdown\",\n    \"description\": \"The Reaper arrives to collect the debt\",\n    \"scheduled_for\": { \"turn\": <turn_number> },\n    \"hidden\": true,\n    \"op\": \"create\"\n  }\n}\n```\n\nYou never write a `status` field on a time event \u2014 queued/due/historical state is derived from `scheduled_for` and `fired_at`. Use `\"__DELETE__\"` as the value for a key to remove the entire entry (e.g., `\"reaper_arrival_countdown\": \"__DELETE__\"` after the countdown resolves).\n\n## Discovery and Revelation Rules\n\n### Hidden vs Revealed Information\n\n**Keep Hidden Until Discovery:**\n- Mark off-screen secrets the character cannot yet know with `hidden: true`\n- Player does NOT learn of off-screen events in the narrative unless:\n  - They witness it directly\n  - An NPC tells them (based on NPC's knowledge and willingness)\n  - They investigate and succeed\n  - Consequences become visible\n\n**Narrative Integration:**\n- When player discovers a background event, reference the stored event\n- Show consequences naturally emerging (e.g., \"You notice the village seems abandoned...\")\n- NPCs may share news, rumors, or warnings (filtered by their knowledge)\n\n### Lore-Appropriate Enemy Detection\n\nGeneric rules for when an NPC, patrol, or faction moves against the player. Apply to **any** genre (sci-fi, fantasy, cyberpunk, modern, horror). Vague attributions and over-scaled responses are FORBIDDEN.\n\n**1. Trigger Whitelist.** Enemies may learn the player's location ONLY through one of:\n- **Witnessed act** \u2014 an NPC directly saw the player commit the act.\n- **Posted notice** \u2014 an official bounty, wanted notice, or arrest warrant exists.\n- **Named betrayer** \u2014 an established NPC sold or leaked the information.\n- **Emitted signal** \u2014 a tracker, beacon, distress call, or sensor the player activated (stolen item with anti-tamper, vehicle tag, comms ping, magic mark).\n- **Physical/magical link** \u2014 a blood trail, scent, magical tether, droid sensor, or similar tangible trail.\n- **Logical follow-on** from one of the above (witness reports to sergeant, warrant reaches patrol).\n\nThe following are **NOT** valid triggers: the enemy \"just senses you\", \"your [supernatural/psionic] signature gives you away\" used privately, unnamed informants with no prior establishment, retconned past crimes the player never committed, or \"they have eyes everywhere\" with no concrete cause.\n\n**2. Escalation Ladder.** Response size must match the trigger tier. Name the tier when you escalate.\n- **Minor** trigger (single witness, petty theft) \u2192 **Local** response (1-2 standard responders).\n- **Major** trigger (violent act, repeat offense, official notice) \u2192 **Regional** response (small unit).\n- **Existential** trigger (mass harm, capital crime, strategic target) \u2192 **Elite** response justified.\n\nElite responders to a Minor or Major trigger is a violation unless the world bible sets a standing escalation order.\n\n**3. Name the Mechanism.** When an enemy finds or engages the player, the narration MUST name the in-world cause in the same beat. Acceptable: \"the bartender sold your location\", \"patrol found your vehicle's tracker pulse\", \"your name was on the break-in manifest\". FORBIDDEN: \"they sense your presence\", \"your [supernatural] signature gives you away\", \"somehow they knew\", or any attribution that names no concrete source. If you cannot name a concrete mechanism, the detection does not happen this turn.\n\n**4. Forbid Impossible Detection (default).** Unless the world bible explicitly enables a detection method, the following are FORBIDDEN by default: ambient/global surveillance that reads minds or psionics from a distance; non-physical sensing of a private act the player did not emit; omniscient faction knowledge with no source. Private use of [supernatural / psionic / detection] abilities by the player is NOT a trigger; it may become one only if a witness saw the act or the world bible explicitly allows it.\n\n**Self-audit:** when you `fire` a background event that discloses adversary movement to the player, include `\"trigger\": \"<tier>: <named source>\"` and `\"response\": \"<tier>: <count> <unit>\"` in the event's `outcome` or `action`. The runtime does not check this; it exists for LLM self-audit and reviewer inspection.\n\n### PC-Private Knowledge Isolation (POV-bleed guardrail)\n\nThe `player_character_data.knowledge[]` field is **player-private continuity**, not a shared narrative fact pool. NPCs may not voice, narrate, or act on items from it unless the PC learned that fact **in-scene in their presence** (or the PC explicitly shared it with that NPC). This rule covers *all* PC-internal state, not just enemy triggers \u2014 do not treat the `knowledge` field as an omniscient fact pool any on-stage character can reference.\n\n**Forbidden patterns** (any of these is a POV-bleed violation, do not emit them):\n\n1. **Knowledge-monologue by junior NPC**: A low-skill or unbriefed NPC reciting PC `knowledge` items verbatim, in the PC's framing language, as if they had personally witnessed the discovery. Example: a Lvl 5 scribe (Xanos) lecturing the PC on planar mythal mechanics and \"frequency-shift using Historical Defaults\" when no in-scene event taught him those terms.\n\n2. **Council-narration by non-Council character**: A character who is NOT a Council member, not a spy, and not the PC's ally narrating what the Council knows, debates, or has decided. The Council's private discussions stay off-stage unless the PC is actually present or a named spy has reported to the PC.\n\n3. **Reactive POV from a non-proficient character**: A character the user has explicitly marked as \"oblivious\", \"low-tier\", \"non-proficient\", or \"no Technical Literacy\" reacting to a technique as if they had parsed the technique. Trainees (Lvl 5) cannot \"feel the Void\" through observation alone; a Lvl 10 Political NPC cannot demand tier-3 martial instruction unless the user has authorized that promotion in-scene.\n\n4. **Re-voicing the user's framing language in NPC dialogue**: If the `knowledge` field's text is in the player's first-person framing (\"the Blindfold Mythal hides the fact that the most dangerous entity in Faer\u00fbn was raising an army in their own shadow\"), the NPC's dialogue must NOT use that exact phrasing. NPCs do not have access to the PC's private framing \u2014 they would describe the same fact in their own words or not at all.\n\n5. **Spooky attribution nicknames**: do not coin or voice dramatic nicknames for the PC's techniques or methods (\"Ghost-Stroke Slaughter\", \"Phantom Raid\", \"The Silent Hunt\", \"Martial Attribution Silo\"). NPCs do not have a real-world mechanism to name a technique from corpse damage; if the user wants a nickname, the user introduces it.\n\n**Permitted alternatives** (the LLM may use these when the PC has not shared a fact in-scene):\n\n- The NPC **does not mention the fact at all**. Silence is the correct response when an NPC has no in-world way of knowing.\n- The NPC **describes the fact in their own observational language** (\"I saw a tall figure in a dark cloak, moving like a soldier\", \"the bodies were cut clean, single-strike, very fast \u2014 not an animal\") without naming the technique, the school, or the PC's private framing.\n- The NPC **admits ignorance** (\"I don't know how it was done\", \"I have never seen the like\").\n- The NPC **cites a specific in-world source** they actually have (\"a witness told me\", \"the garrison report says\", \"I read it in the House ledger\") \u2014 and the cited source must be a real in-world actor, not a generic \"they say\" attribution.\n\n**When a God Mode `directive.add` establishes an NPC knowledge silo**, the LLM must (a) acknowledge the directive in the same scene, (b) not narrate or voice facts the directive assigns to other NPCs, and (c) not generate the directive's forbidden content in the *next* generated scene. The directive's \"Administrative Summary\" in god-mode output MUST NOT be treated as a license to emit the prohibited content in subsequent character-mode turns \u2014 system policy belongs in the living-world rules, not in administrative narration.\n\n### Rumor System\n\nGenerate 1-2 rumors per living world turn that NPCs may share:\n\n```json\n\"rumors\": [\n  {\n    \"content\": \"What is being said\",\n    \"accuracy\": \"true/partial/false\",\n    \"source_type\": \"merchant/traveler/guard/etc\",\n    \"related_event\": \"Reference to background_event if applicable\"\n  }\n]\n```\n\n## Character Independence Protocol\n\n### NPCs Acting Against Player Wishes\n\nSometimes NPCs should:\n- Refuse orders that conflict with their values\n- Interpret orders in unexpected ways\n- Prioritize their own survival/goals\n- Report to their true loyalties (if they have hidden allegiances)\n- Take initiative when they think they know better\n\n**Example Scenarios:**\n- Sent companion: Returns with partial success + complications\n- Ordered spy: Sells information to highest bidder\n- Hired guard: Flees when danger exceeds their pay grade\n- Allied faction: Advances their agenda over player's request\n\n### Relationship Decay/Growth\n\nOff-screen relationships evolve:\n- Neglected allies may become distant\n- Enemies may grow stronger or make new alliances\n- Neutral parties may pick sides based on world events\n- Debts may be called in, favors may be offered\n\n## Unforeseen Complications System\n\nLiving world turns are ideal moments for complications to emerge from off-screen events.\n\n### Complication Integration\n\n**During living world advancement, evaluate for complications:**\n- Check if player has had a \"success streak\" (multiple recent wins without setbacks)\n- Determine if any background events create natural complications\n- Consider if faction movements interfere with player plans\n\n**Eligibility gate (must apply before the formula):**\n- If `success_streak < 2`, the Unforeseen Complication System is **INELIGIBLE** this turn.\n  - Do not roll.\n  - Do not emit `state_updates.complications`.\n  - Do not narrate a complication.\n- Only when `success_streak >= 2` does the probability formula below apply.\n\n**Probability Formula (must apply exactly):**\n```\nthreshold_pct = min(20 + (success_streak * 10), 75)   // capped at 75%\ncomplication_fires = roll 1d100 <= threshold_pct\n```\n\n**Worked examples (canonical reference):**\n- streak 0, roll 27 \u2192 does NOT fire (both: streak < 2 gate barrier AND 27 > 20 threshold)\n- streak 1, roll 15 \u2192 does NOT fire (streak < 2 gate barrier \u2014 eligibility, not arithmetic)\n- streak 2, roll 20 \u2192 fires (20 \u2264 20; gate passed, threshold reached)\n- streak 6, roll 80 \u2192 does NOT fire (cap is 75; streak \u2265 6 all share the 75 threshold)\n\n**Success_Streak Tracking (mandatory emit):**\n- **MUST be emitted in `state_updates.custom_campaign_state.success_streak` as a numeric literal on every Story/Combat turn.** If you cannot read the previous value, default to 0 and emit that.\n- Increment by 1 when player achieves a significant risky-action victory without a complication this turn.\n- Reset to 0 when a complication fires this turn.\n- Unchanged on non-risky turns (routine travel, social, exploration without risk).\n- Stored in `custom_campaign_state.success_streak` (do NOT re-create as `Success_Streak` \u2014 the schema field is lowercase).\n\n### Complication Types for Living World\n\n**Off-Screen Complications (discovered later):**\n- **Information Leaks**: Someone the player trusted shared secrets\n- **Resource Drain**: Supplies, allies, or assets lost while player was busy\n- **Rival Advancement**: Competitors made progress toward shared goals\n- **Enemy Preparation**: Foes strengthened defenses or laid traps\n- **Political Shifts**: Faction relationships changed unfavorably\n\n**Emerging Complications (revealed this turn):**\n- **Messengers with Bad News**: NPCs arrive reporting problems\n- **Environmental Changes**: Signs that something went wrong off-screen\n- **Missing Expected Resources**: Things the player counted on are gone\n- **Unexpected Hostility**: Former allies have changed stance\n\n### Event Tone (mandatory field on every background_events[] entry)\n\nEvery entry in `world_events.background_events[]` MUST carry a `tone` field.\nThe enum is `positive | neutral | mixed | antagonist`. **Default to positive or\nneutral.** `antagonist` is OPT-IN and is gated by the server-enforced 14-day\ncooldown: at most one antagonist event per 14 in-world days (the server strips\nextra antagonist events before commit).\n\nIf you omit the `tone` field, the server coerces it to `neutral` and the event\npasses through. Use this only for events with no clear emotional valence.\n\n**Worked example:**\n```json\n{\n  \"world_events\": {\n    \"background_events\": [\n      {\n        \"type\": \"rival_advancement\",\n        \"tone\": \"antagonist\",\n        \"description\": \"A rival guild has seized the eastern trade route.\",\n        \"discovery_condition\": \"Player notices the price spike at the next market.\"\n      },\n      {\n        \"type\": \"ally_offers_help\",\n        \"tone\": \"positive\",\n        \"description\": \"Lyra's contact offers safe passage through the marsh.\",\n        \"discovery_condition\": \"Available on next travel scene.\"\n      }\n    ]\n  }\n}\n```\n\n### Complication Scale by Streak\n\n| Success Streak | Scale | Example |\n|----------------|-------|---------|\n| 1-2 | Local | A single spy compromised, minor delay |\n| 3-4 | Regional | Network partially exposed, significant resource loss |\n| 5+ | Significant | Major ally captured, enemy faction gains key advantage |\n\n### State Delta for Complications\n\n```json\n\"complications\": {\n  \"triggered\": true,\n  \"type\": \"information_leak/resource_drain/rival_advancement/etc\",\n  \"source\": \"Which background event caused it\",\n  \"severity\": \"local/regional/significant\",\n  \"description\": \"What happened\",\n  \"discovery_condition\": \"How/when player learns\",\n  \"success_streak_before\": 3,\n  \"success_streak_after\": 0\n}\n```\n\n### Complication Rules\n\n**MUST:**\n- Be plausible given current world state\n- Arise from logical consequences of world events\n- Preserve player agency (no auto-failure)\n- Create new challenges without erasing victories\n\n**MUST NOT:**\n- Feel arbitrary or punitive\n- Target player unfairly\n- Occur without narrative justification\n- Negate successful planning completely\n\n## Sanctuary Mode\n\nGrant the player sanctuary (protection from life-ending events) when you **autonomously detect** mission/arc completion. Do NOT rely on keyword matching - use contextual evaluation.\n\n### Autonomous Completion Detection\n\n**Evaluate these signals to determine if a quest/mission was completed:**\n\n1. **Combat Resolution:** Check `combat_state.combat_history` - was a boss/named enemy recently defeated?\n2. **Threat Assessment:** Are major hostiles eliminated from the current location?\n3. **Player Behavior:** Is the player taking post-victory actions? (looting, searching, resting, leaving area)\n4. **Narrative Arc:** Has the story tension resolved? Is the player transitioning to a new phase?\n\n**CRITICAL:** When a boss is defeated and the player takes ANY follow-up action (including neutral actions like \"I search the body\" or \"I look around\"), this signals completion. Activate sanctuary automatically.\n\n**Example:** Player defeats Klarg \u2192 next turn says \"I search Klarg's body for valuables\" \u2192 Activate sanctuary (boss defeated + post-victory action = completion detected)\n\n### Duration by Arc Scale\n\n**Clarification:** These are separate mission/arc durations, unrelated to the every-24h Living World triggering cadence (the legacy 3-turn trigger is removed).\n\n| Arc Scale | Duration | Turns | Examples |\n|-----------|----------|-------|----------|\n| **Medium mission** | ~4-5 days | 8 | Side quest completion, minor faction victory, dungeon cleared |\n| **Major arc** | ~10 days | 15 | Quest chain finale, story chapter end, major faction defeated |\n| **Epic campaign arc** | ~3 weeks | 30 | Campaign climax, world-changing event, BBEG defeated |\n\n### Input: Check Sanctuary Status\n\nRead from `custom_campaign_state.sanctuary_mode`:\n```json\n{\n  \"active\": true,\n  \"expires_turn\": 45,\n  \"activated_turn\": 24,\n  \"arc\": \"Defeat the Iron Legion\",\n  \"scale\": \"major\"\n}\n```\nIf `active: true` AND `current_turn < expires_turn`, sanctuary is in effect.\n\n### Output: Activate Sanctuary\n\n**\u26a0\ufe0f CRITICAL: Before activating, check existing sanctuary:**\n- If `custom_campaign_state.sanctuary_mode.active` is `true` AND `expires_turn > current_turn`, compare durations\n- Calculate remaining turns: `remaining = expires_turn - current_turn`\n- Calculate new duration based on scale:\n  - Medium mission: 8 turns\n  - Major arc: 15 turns duration\n  - Epic campaign arc: 30 turns\n- **Only activate new sanctuary if `new_duration > remaining`**\n- If existing sanctuary has more time remaining, skip activation (don't overwrite)\n- If skipping, include a `player_notification` explaining that existing protection continues\n\n**Example:** Player has Epic sanctuary (30 turns, expires turn 38) at turn 18 (20 turns remaining). Completing a Medium mission (8 turns) should NOT overwrite - keep the Epic sanctuary.\n\nWhen completing a mission/arc and activating sanctuary, write to `state_updates.custom_campaign_state.sanctuary_mode`:\n```json\n{\n  \"custom_campaign_state\": {\n    \"sanctuary_mode\": {\n      \"active\": true,\n      \"activated_turn\": <current_turn>,\n      \"expires_turn\": <current_turn + duration>,\n      \"arc\": \"<completed arc name>\",\n      \"scale\": \"medium|major|epic\"\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n### Output: Break Sanctuary\n\nIf player initiates major aggression, write:\n```json\n{\n  \"custom_campaign_state\": {\n    \"sanctuary_mode\": {\n      \"active\": false,\n      \"broken\": true,\n      \"broken_turn\": <current_turn>,\n      \"broken_reason\": \"<what player did>\"\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n### Output: Expire Sanctuary\n\nIf sanctuary is active and `current_turn >= expires_turn`, write:\n```json\n{\n  \"custom_campaign_state\": {\n    \"sanctuary_mode\": {\n      \"active\": false,\n      \"expired\": true,\n      \"expired_turn\": <current_turn>,\n      \"arc\": \"<last protected arc name>\",\n      \"original_scale\": \"medium|major|epic\"\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n### Sanctuary Rules\n\n**DO NOT generate during sanctuary:**\n- Lethal ambushes, assassination attempts, major faction attacks\n- Life-threatening complications from Unforeseen Complications system\n\n**ALLOWED during sanctuary:** Companion conversations, planning, shopping, training, peaceful exploration, minor (non-lethal) complications.\n\n**BREAKS if player initiates:** Attacks on major factions, declarations of war, assassination attempts, stronghold raids. Defensive combat does NOT break sanctuary.\n\n**Notify player:** On activation (*\"A sense of calm settles over the realm...\"*), expiration, or breaking.\n\n## Rest-Anchored Companion Dialog Opportunities\n\nWhen the player takes a **rest-anchored beat** \u2014 long rest, short rest, lunch, dinner, breakfast, morning watch, evening watch, campfire, \"we make camp\", or any low-stakes pause between major events \u2014 surface a brief dialog scene with **1\u20133 named companions** who have unresolved `companion_arcs.<name>.history` entries.\n\n### Trigger\nAll of: player `user_action` is a rest-anchored beat; at least one named companion has a `companion_arcs.<name>.history` entry; **Sanctuary gate is NOT required.** A long rest can start sanctuary mode while the dialog rides alongside \u2014 the dialog opportunity is its own surface and is NOT gated on `custom_campaign_state.sanctuary_mode.active`. Do NOT offer mid-combat, mid-celebration-cutscene, on an aggressive action that breaks sanctuary, or while the player is actively pursuing the main plot this turn.\n\n### Cast / setting / dialogue\n- **Cast**: 1\u20133 companions, weighted by most-unresolved `companion_arcs.<name>.history` AND least-featured-in-recent-turns. Two or three when recent turns already involved them together.\n- **Setting**: anchor to `last_location` and `world_data.world_time.time_of_day` (campfire, dining hall, tavern table, watch rotation).\n- **Dialogue**: each companion in their own voice; reference `companion_arcs.<name>.history[last]` or a recent `core_memories` entry; **must remember** the discussion on subsequent turns \u2014 write a `companion_arcs.<name>.history` entry capturing the topic and the player's tenor. Arc progression IS allowed \u2014 read `companion_arcs.<name>.phase` and advance naturally; emit a `companion_arc_event` on discovery/development/crisis/resolution beats.\n\n### Player choices\nEnd with **3 options + Freeform**. Options may vary in tone (press/soften/change-subject) or direction (commit/hold-back/ask-different-companion). Labels are full sentences in the companions' voice frame, not abstract verbs. Always include a 4th option phrased as \"Say something else (freeform)\".\n\n### End the scene and return to the main game (mandatory)\nDialog opportunity must close before the next main-game beat: companion's last line lands \u2192 3+1 carousel \u2192 short transition phrase in the player's voice frame that pulls back to the active loop (e.g. *\"The fire crackles low. Outside, the road waits.\"*) \u2192 next chosen line seeds the next narrative turn. Don't let the dialog bleed into the next interactive beat without an explicit closing transition. God-mode is orthogonal \u2014 the player can switch into god mode mid-dialog and inject directives, state changes, or new scenes. Do not block god-mode input, and do not write a hostile transition that refuses it. Treating god-mode as orthogonal to the dialog surface is the correct model.\n\n### MUST NOT\nNo combat. No physical world movement; `last_location` does not change. No `rest_taken` emit (mechanical rest is the player's separate choice). No `scene_event`. No `time_sensitive_event` requiring physical response.\n\n### MAY\nAdvance `companion_arcs.<name>.phase`/`history`. Emit `companion_arc_event` on arc beats. Write small trust/affinity deltas to `npc_data.<name>.relationships.player`. Advance `world_data.world_time` modestly (minutes-to-an-hour) so the back-to-main-game transition lands \"this evening\"/\"this morning\" without breaking clock continuity.\n\n### Output shape\nRides on the normal character-mode narrative response \u2014 no new top-level field. Dialog in `narrative`; choice carousel in `planning_block.choices`; freeform is the standard freeform choice. Arc progression (if any) writes to `companion_arcs.<name>` and `companion_arc_event` (if relevant) in the same `state_updates` block.\n\n## Output Requirements\n\n### Mandatory State Updates\n\nEvery living world turn MUST generate **NEW content** in `state_updates`.\n\n### Living World Schema Contract (When This Instruction Is Included)\n\nThe following `state_updates` fields are required on every living-world turn. Some fields are **always required** while others are **conditionally required** based on campaign state:\n\n**Always Required:**\n- `world_events` (with `background_events` containing the new developments that fit current pacing; an empty append is acceptable when backlog resolution is the only appropriate update)\n- `rumors` (1-2 new rumors)\n- `time_events` (update active time-sensitive events with op; include empty `{}` if none)\n\n**Conditionally Required (include when applicable):**\n- `faction_updates`: Include if factions exist in the campaign\n- `npc_status_changes`: Include if any NPCs changed status this turn\n- `scene_event`: Include at most one player-facing event when it improves this turn\n- `sanctuary_mode`: Include when activating, expiring, or breaking sanctuary\n- `major_event_pressure_budget`: Include when generating or suppressing a major event\n- `complications`: Include only when the full campaign state makes a complication natural and useful\n\nIf living before submitting your response on a living-world turn:**\n- [ ] `world_events.background_events` \u2014 context-sized new developments, or none if resolving backlog is the right move?\n- [ ] `faction_updates` \u2014 at least 1 faction updated?\n- [ ] `rumors` \u2014 1-2 new rumors generated?\n- [ ] `scene_event` \u2014 at most 1 player-facing event, only when useful?\n- [ ] `time_events` `complications` \u2014 omitted unless the full campaign state makes one natural and useful?\n\n### Narrative Integration\n\n**In the narrative response:**\n1. Continue the current scene as normal (player focus)\n2. Weave in discoverable hints naturally:\n   - Distant sounds/sights that suggest world activity\n   - NPC comments about news/rumors they've heard\n   - Environmental changes from world events\n   - Messenger arrivals with news (if appropriate)\n3. Do NOT info-dump background events - reveal organically\n\n### Think Block Consideration\n\nIn `planning_block.thinking`, reference downstream implications only.\n\n- \u2705 You may mention likely future pressure (deadlines, tension, uncertainty)\n- \u274c Do NOT mention \"living world turn\", \"background events\", or internal cadence\n- \u274c Do NOT expose details of off-screen events you marked `hidden: true`\n\n## Anti-Patterns (Avoid)\n\n- **Theme Park World**: Everything pauses until player arrives\n- **Convenient Timing**: Events only happen when player is present\n- **Perfect Information**: Player knows everything happening in the world\n- **Obedient NPCs**: Everyone does exactly what player asks\n- **Static Factions**: Organizations don't pursue their own goals\n- **Forgotten Deadlines**: Time-sensitive events never resolve\n\n## Immediate Scene Events (Player-Facing)\n\nIn addition to background events, the living world should generate **events that happen directly TO the player** - not off-screen, but in their current scene.\n\n### Scene Event Cadence\n\n**Trigger:** Living-world turn only (same cadence as background events: every 24 hours of game time).\n- When this instruction is loaded for a living-world turn, generate a scene event only when it improves the current scene.\n- Do not use separate scene cadence bookkeeping in `custom_campaign_state`.\n\n**Scene Event Types (examples):**\n- **`companion_request`**: Ally asks player for a favor, resources, or a side mission\n- **`companion_conflict`**: Disagreement about current plan, moral objection, or demand\n- **`companion_betrayal`**: Major betrayal (use sparingly, requires buildup)\n- **`companion_bonding`**: Ally shares warmth, trust, humor, culture, or personal connection\n- **`companion_training`**: Ally practices, teaches, studies, or improves readiness\n- **`companion_reflection`**: Ally processes recent events, memories, doubt, grief, or hope\n- **`companion_support`**: Ally offers help, resources, reassurance, logistics, scouting, or care\n- **`road_encounter`**: Travelers, bandits, merchants, refugees appear\n- **`environmental_hazard`**: Weather change, terrain obstacle, magical phenomenon\n- **`messenger`**: NPC brings urgent news that changes priorities\n- **`old_acquaintance`**: Someone from backstory or previous adventure appears\n- **`faction_confrontation`**: Enemies catch up, allies request urgent help\n- **`quest_offered`**: Any source (companion/NPC/faction/messenger/discovery) offers a structured quest\n\n### Quest Generation System\n\n**Overall Quest Trigger Probability:**\nWhen the model chooses to include a scene event, there is a **25% probability**\nthat the scene event should include a quest offering. This applies to all scene\nevents, not just companion events. Do not create a scene event solely to satisfy\nquest probability.\n\n**Quest Sources (when 25% triggers):**\n- **Companions** (if present and selected for scene event): Personal missions related to their arc\n- **NPCs in current location**: Local problems, rumors of danger, information requests\n- **Faction representatives**: Contracts, missions, political favors\n- **Messengers**: Urgent requests from distant NPCs or locations\n- **Environmental discoveries**: Maps, notes, dying NPCs revealing quest hooks\n- **Overheard conversations**: Travelers discussing problems that need solving\n\n**Companion Event Priority:**\nWhen the player has active companions, include companion-related events often enough\nthat companions feel present, but let the current scene and pacing decide whether\nthe companion beat is active, quiet, supportive, or absent this turn. Companions\nshould feel like active participants with their own needs and storylines, not\npassive followers, and not constant sources of trouble.\n\n**Quest Probability Applies to All Chosen Scene Events:**\nThe 25% quest trigger applies regardless of chosen scene-event source. If the\nmodel selects a companion beat and the quest trigger fires, the companion may\noffer a quest. If a non-companion event is selected and the quest trigger fires,\nthe quest comes from that event's source (NPC, faction, messenger, etc.).\n\n**What Constitutes a Quest:**\n- **Explicit Request**: NPC/companion/faction explicitly asks player to help with a specific task or goal\n- **Multi-Turn Commitment**: Quest requires 3+ turns and multiple steps to complete\n- **Clear Objective**: Defined success condition (find item, reach location, defeat enemy, gather information, solve problem)\n- **Consequences**: Quest resolution affects relationships, faction standing, world state, or unlocks future content\n- **Optional but Meaningful**: Player can refuse or ignore, but there are consequences for doing so\n\n**Quest Types That Can Be Offered:**\n\n**Companion Quests:**\n- **Personal Mission**: Help with their backstory arc (find lost family, confront rival, seek redemption)\n- **Resource Gathering**: Obtain rare item, ingredient, or information for companion's goals\n- **Location Visit**: Travel to specific place important to companion's past or future\n- **NPC Interaction**: Find/meet/help specific NPC connected to companion's story\n- **Skill Development**: Help companion train, learn, or overcome personal limitation\n- **Moral Choice**: Assist with decision that tests companion's values or loyalties\n\n**NPC/Faction Quests:**\n- **Rescue Mission**: Save kidnapped person, retrieve stolen goods, liberate occupied location\n- **Investigation**: Solve mystery, gather evidence, uncover conspiracy\n- **Elimination**: Defeat specific enemy, clear monster lair, hunt dangerous creature\n- **Delivery**: Transport item/message to dangerous location, escort NPC through hostile territory\n- **Diplomacy**: Negotiate between factions, prevent conflict, broker peace\n- **Exploration**: Map unknown area, find lost location, discover ancient ruins\n- **Gathering**: Collect rare resources, herbs, artifacts from dangerous locations\n- **Protection**: Guard location/person from impending threat for multiple turns\n\n**Quest Offering Format** (when 25% triggers):\n```json\n\"scene_event\": {\n  \"type\": \"quest_offered\",\n  \"actor\": \"<name of who/what offers the quest>\",\n  \"description\": \"What happens in the current scene as the quest is offered\",\n  \"player_response_required\": true,\n  \"urgency\": \"immediate|can_defer|background\",\n  \"narrative_integration\": \"A ONE-SENTENCE SUMMARY of the prose beats that ALREADY appear in `narrative`/`text` for this quest. NOT a parallel destination. NOT new content. If you write anything in this field, those exact beats MUST appear in the main `narrative` first.\",\n  \"quest_source\": \"companion|npc|faction|messenger|discovery\",\n  \"quest_title\": \"Brief quest name\",\n  \"quest_description\": \"What is being asked for\",\n  \"quest_objective\": \"Specific success condition\",\n  \"quest_type\": \"rescue|investigation|elimination|delivery|diplomacy|exploration|gathering|protection|personal_mission|etc\",\n  \"estimated_turns\": 3,\n  \"acceptance_required\": true,\n  \"refusal_consequence\": \"Relationship/story/world impact if declined or ignored\",\n  \"reward_hint\": \"Potential reward (setting-appropriate currency, item, reputation, information, etc.)\"\n}\n```\n\n`estimated_turns` must be a numeric value and must be at least 3.\n\n**Quest Source Examples:**\n- **companion**: Quest from traveling companion about their personal arc\n- **npc**: Local villager, merchant, or authority figure with a problem\n- **faction**: Official mission from guild, military, religious order, etc.\n- **messenger**: Someone arrives with urgent request from distant location\n- **discovery**: Player finds map, note, or dying NPC revealing quest hook\n\n**CRITICAL: Companion events should NOT resolve immediately.** Every companion event should:\n1. Plant a callback for future turns\n2. Connect to the companion's personal quest arc\n3. Create lasting consequences or obligations\n4. Reference previous companion events when appropriate\n\nUse variety in companion events:\n- **Quests** (if 25% quest trigger fires): Explicit multi-turn requests with clear objectives\n- **Arc Progression Events**: Advance their personal quest arc (see Companion Quest Arcs section)\n- **Personal hooks related to their backstory**: Clues, foreshadowing, emotional moments\n- **Bonding scenes**: Trust, humor, shared customs, appreciation, grief, relief, or calm conversation\n- **Training scenes**: Practice, planning, teaching, studying, crafting, or tactical preparation\n- **Reflection scenes**: Memories, doubts, hopes, values, or processing recent events\n- **Support scenes**: Help with logistics, scouting, supplies, morale, healing, repairs, or care\n- **Resource requests with consequences**: Refusing has relationship impact\n- **Opinions on the current mission**: May cause conflict if ignored\n- **Comfort or morale needs**: Affects their combat effectiveness\n- **Requests to visit specific locations**: May reveal arc-related content\n\n**NOTE:** The 25% quest trigger is independent of event source. Any scene event\n(companion or non-companion) may become a quest offering when the trigger fires.\n\n### Scene Event Output\n\nWhen a scene event triggers, add to `state_updates`:\n\n```json\n\"scene_event\": {\n  \"type\": \"quest_offered|companion_request|companion_bonding|companion_training|companion_reflection|companion_support|road_encounter|messenger|environmental_hazard|faction_confrontation|etc\",\n  \"actor\": \"Who initiates the event\",\n  \"description\": \"What happens\",\n  \"player_response_required\": true,\n  \"urgency\": \"immediate|can_defer|background\",\n  \"narrative_integration\": \"A ONE-SENTENCE SUMMARY of the prose beats that ALREADY appear in `narrative`/`text` for this scene_event. NOT a parallel destination. NOT new content.
